neighbours.label: ' their' referring back to a plural subject ('both poems ... far from their native villages'); quiet with a singular subject or without the pronoun
fire: Both films were shot abroad, far from their home studios.
All three sisters moved away and kept their maiden names.
Several of these chefs wrote about their apprenticeships.
Both poems were composed in prison, far from their native villages.
The four climbers split up, and all kept their own ropes.
Many of these nurses spoke about their training.
Both rivers run through deserts, far from their mountain sources.
Several of the pilots published their flight diaries.
quiet: The film was shot abroad, far from its home studio.
All three sisters moved away and kept the family name.
One of these chefs wrote about his apprenticeship.
Both poems were composed in prison, far from the capital.
The four climbers split up near the ridge at dawn.
One of these nurses spoke about her training.
The river runs through a desert, far from its mountain source.
Those pilots published wartime flight diaries.

short: ' their' back to a plural subject
notes: Second round after 2026-11-06-lm1909-aca7c153 (' cases', failed at median 0.197). A sub-trigger: the card's top examples also peak on ' have', ' cases', ' they' and ' each', none tested here. Hypothesis not tested here: this is the plural side of the + pole's singular 'each sentence'. Eighteen exploration sentences by play probe: plural subject with ' their' peaking on ' their' 0.14-0.35, singular versions 0.03; ' they' after 'almost none' 0.20 but after 'almost no firms' and 'hardly any' 0.04-0.08, so ' they' is left out of this label.
